stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals a significant reliance of generative AI data centers on natural gas.
The report highlights intense competition for power supply and suitable data center locations as the AI boom accelerates.
This underscores the growing, often overlooked, environmental and infrastructural footprint of large-scale AI development.

stories.title: OpenAI Rolls Out GPT-6.1 Terra Across ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI has released a new model iteration, GPT-6.1 Terra.
The new model emphasizes enhanced visual reasoning capabilities.
GPT-6.1 Terra is being integrated across ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API.

stories.author: unknown

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, tool calling, and context gathering on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial community of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Highway thieves exploited GPS spoofing technology to execute a large-scale theft.
The stolen cargo was high-value data center equipment, indicating a critical supply chain vulnerability.
The incident highlights significant security risks in logistics and transportation infrastructure.

stories.title: Tesla gave up the EV crown. Now it wants to win the autonomy race.
stories.author: Kana Inagaki, Financial Times
bullet_points: Tesla is shifting strategic focus from dominating the EV market to leading the autonomous driving race.
The company is betting heavily on autonomy subscriptions as a key driver for future profitability and margins.
This pivot suggests a strategic move to diversify revenue streams beyond traditional vehicle sales.

stories.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to a quarter of its workforce
stories.author: mooreds
bullet_points: Microsoft is implementing voluntary buyouts for a portion of its workforce.
This indicates potential internal restructuring or strategic shifts within the tech giant.
The news reflects broader industry trends regarding workforce optimization in large tech firms.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial supported model is Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech functionality.
The implementation offers fast, real-time streaming of speech generation, achieving speeds over 100x real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now accessible via Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is available for free for a limited promotional period via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud computing environment.
This combination addresses the need for secure deployment of local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: The RealReal is enhancing its bot defense system to prevent AI agents from exploiting its platform.
The update is a direct response to reports that AI agents could abuse the retailer's item reserve system.
This highlights the growing challenge of automated scraping and bot activity in e-commerce, particularly in luxury resale.

stories.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo display ‘issue’ after reports of cracked screens
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has officially acknowledged a display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units.
The reported issue involves cracked or broken inner screens, sometimes displaying a bright line.
The acknowledgment was made in a statement provided to Bloomberg and 9to5Mac.

stories.title: Five weird details from Anthropic’s IPO filing
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic has officially filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC, signaling its impending IPO.
The filing provides detailed insights into the company's financials, executive compensation, and spending plans.
The document outlines various risks associated with Anthropic's business and future ambitions.

stories.title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple has released an updated iPad mini.
The key hardware upgrade is the inclusion of a larger OLED screen.
The new model is priced at $700, and Apple touts it as a major line update.

stories.title: Musk accuses Ukraine of violating Starlink terms with deadly drone strikes
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Elon Musk alleges Ukraine violated Starlink terms through drone strikes.
Ukraine disputes the claims, stating Starshield operations are normal.
The dispute centers on the use of Starlink's commercial service during military operations.

stories.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
stories.author: Shenji Wan
bullet_points: SceneBloom is a new agentic framework designed to generate realistic and diverse indoor environments for embodied AI agents.
It addresses the challenge of precise spatial grounding by combining visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D scene generation.
The research aims to improve generalizable embodied learning by providing high-quality, simulation-ready environments.

stories.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
stories.author: Laixi Shi
bullet_points: Introduces RobustRLlib, a unified library and benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses key limitations in existing robust RL: poor algorithm reusability and unclear empirical boundaries.
Integrates 17 representative robust online RL algorithms to facilitate broader research and deployment.

stories.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: DexPort introduces a portable interface designed to solve the bottleneck of collecting high-quality data for dexterous manipulation.
It aims to bridge the gap between complex teleoperation setups and the ambiguity of human motion demonstrations.
The system facilitates direct, hands-on data collection for training robotic systems to perform intricate tasks.

stories.title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Zhongliang Jiang
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of integrating continuous numerical data (like medical measurements) into discrete token-based Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
Introduces HAD-VLM, a hybrid framework combining autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction.
Applies the model to prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement, enhancing the utility of VLMs in medical imaging.

stories.title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms
stories.author: Tianjun Feng
bullet_points: Examines the economic trade-offs for LLM platforms balancing ad revenue against subscription fees.
Models a monopolistic platform optimizing response quality, ad intensity, and pricing simultaneously.
Suggests that advertising can potentially finance useful service features when ad-supported and ad-free tiers coexist.

stories.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
stories.author: Armon Rasooli
bullet_points: Introduces Yalda Embedding, a new 595.8-million-parameter dense retrieval model specifically for the Persian language.
Addresses the challenge of limited language-specific training resources for Persian NLP tasks.
Achieves the highest macro-average among evaluated 0.6B models on eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB.

stories.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
stories.author: Bernhard Bauer
bullet_points: Challenges the assumption that performance-optimized code from LLMs inherently means lower energy consumption.
Empirically evaluates if LLM self-refinement pipelines produce energy-efficient code compared to human benchmarks.
Investigates the trade-off between the energy cost of the optimization process and subsequent energy savings.

stories.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Tajana Rosing
bullet_points: NgramRL addresses the high computational cost (over 70% of training time) associated with autoregressive rollout generation in RL post-training for LLMs.
The paper proposes a novel method, Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding, to accelerate this process.
It specifically tackles limitations of existing speculative decoding methods, such as GPU memory constraints in model-based drafters and lack of repetition exploitation in model-free approaches.

stories.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
stories.author: Laixi Shi
bullet_points: Introduces RobustRLlib, a new library and benchmark specifically designed for Robust Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses two key limitations in current robust RL research: poor algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical performance boundary.
Integrates 17 representative robust online RL algorithms to facilitate broader research and real-world deployment testing.

stories.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: DexPort is a new portable interface designed to address the bottleneck of collecting high-quality data for dexterous manipulation tasks.
It aims to bridge the gap between traditional teleoperation (complex setup) and human demonstrations (requiring estimation/retargeting).
The technology facilitates direct, hands-on data collection of executable robot actions in a portable manner.

stories.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
stories.author: Egor Bondarev
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of few-shot anomaly detection in industrial settings where only a few normal examples are available.
Introduces Flownomaly, which reframes the problem as normal-counterpart recovery within the frozen DINOv2 feature space.
Employs conditional flow matching over patch tokens to learn a velocity field, enabling noise transport toward the normal distribution.

stories.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
stories.author: Federico Lucca
bullet_points: Introduces 'Foyer,' a self-hosted personal inbox agent designed for multilingual message routing and decision-making.
Addresses a critical gap in AI evaluation by proposing a rigorous measurement protocol to establish ground truth *before* model training.
Compares a new 'Typed Decision Model' against a classical baseline and a Generative LLM for inbox triage tasks.

stories.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Ruosong Wang
bullet_points: The paper addresses instability in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Large Language Models (LLMs) caused by discrepancies between inference and training implementations.
The core finding suggests that stabilizing RL can be achieved by aligning only specific parts of the execution stack, rather than requiring full stack alignment or global precision changes.
This research offers a targeted, potentially more efficient remedy for implementation-induced training instability when using BF16 tensors in LLM RL.

stories.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
stories.author: Thierry Tambe
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models when encountering out-of-distribution states during robotic manipulation.
Introduces 'Backtrack,' a lightweight mechanism for failure detection and recovery in frozen VLAs.
The method avoids costly solutions like recovery demonstrations or full policy retraining by using a small failure prediction head.

stories.title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
stories.author: Nikos Zarifis
bullet_points: The research addresses the PAC learning problem for positive linear combinations of ReLU activations in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
A novel algorithm is presented that achieves fully-polynomial time complexity for this learning task.
The algorithm's efficiency is characterized by requiring $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/\varepsilon)$ samples and running time.

stories.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
stories.author: Brian DePasquale
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenging problem of state inference and parameter learning in nonlinear filtering.
It focuses on solving the Zakai equation, a complex Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) governing the unnormalized filtering distribution.
The proposed method, ZENO, utilizes Neural Operators to tackle the high-dimensional nature of these SPDEs, relevant to engineering and neuroscience.

stories.title: The Language of Instruction: Genre and Generative AI
stories.author: James E. Dobson
bullet_points: The paper proposes that instruction-fine-tuned language models operate within a specific 'instructional-conversational genre'.
This genre is defined as a blend of discursive language derived from recursive human-AI conversations.
The instantiation of this genre is achieved through instruction fine-tuning, system prompts, and structured input formatting.

stories.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
stories.author: Federico Lucca
bullet_points: Introduces 'Foyer,' a self-hosted personal inbox agent designed for multilingual message routing.
Addresses the critical issue of unmeasured error rates in personal AI agents where labels are system-generated.
Proposes a rigorous measurement protocol (stratified sampling, human review loop) to establish ground truth *before* training.

stories.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
stories.author: Armon Rasooli
bullet_points: Introduces Yalda Embedding, a new Persian retrieval model designed to address resource limitations in the language.
The model is adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and trained on over one million query-document pairs.
Achieves the highest macro-average among evaluated 0.6B models on eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB.

stories.title: J-Comm: Jacobian-Guided Latent Communication between LLM Agents
stories.author: Saman Halgamuge
bullet_points: Introduces J-Comm, a framework designed to facilitate latent communication between Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
Features GEAR (Geometric Agreement for Latent Reasoning), a training-free method that reweights token candidates to optimize geometric consensus in embedding space.
The framework addresses the need for both continuous reasoning and an interface for external models to leverage intermediate LLM computations.

stories.title: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
stories.author: Constantin Venhoff
bullet_points: Addresses the critical security vulnerability of model backdoors introduced by poisoned training data.
Introduces TopKLoRA, an interpretable variant of LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
Aims to enable 'faithful circuit discovery' by making fine-tuning changes transparent and localizable.

stories.title: Communicating with the Entire Population: Machine Translation of Emergency Alerts and Warnings
stories.author: William D. Lewis
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for multilingual communication during emergencies to reach all affected populations.
It investigates the reliability and adequacy of commercial Machine Translation tools used by emergency response managers.
The study involves a nationwide survey of emergency managers to gauge their experience with automated translation in crisis situations.

stories.title: Sebastian Raschka's from-scratch video course on building reasoning models
stories.author: sgiannopoulos
bullet_points: Sebastian Raschka is offering a video course focused on building reasoning models.
The course emphasizes a 'from-scratch' approach to model development.
The topic falls within the niche but highly relevant area of advanced AI/ML.

stories.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
stories.author: support.apple.com via freddyb
bullet_points: The news concerns the compromise of intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs) belonging to eMudhra.
This is a significant security vulnerability impacting digital trust and authentication systems.
The source (Lobsters) suggests a technical discussion around the implications of this CA compromise.

stories.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra Brings Lower-Cost Computer Use to Visual Workflows
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6.1 Terra, a new model in the GPT-6.1 family.
The model is specifically designed for fast and efficient visual workflows.
A key feature highlighted is its positioning to bring lower-cost computer use to visual tasks.
